sections.title: Everything from this unit, at the counter
sections.content: A pharmacy visit chains together most of what this unit has taught: naming a tünet, asking Van valami X ellen?, and understanding dosage instructions with the kell you already know from A1 plus a new infinitive, bevenni ("to take", of medicine).

items.spanish: Fáj a torkom, és lázam van. Van valami láz ellen?
items.english: My throat hurts, and I have a fever. Is there something for fever?

items.spanish: Tessék, ez egy jó tabletta. Naponta háromszor kell bevenni.
items.english: Here you go, this is a good tablet. It needs to be taken three times a day.

sections.content: naponta ("daily") uses the same -nta/-nte ending you met for mindennap-type frequency early in A2 — naponta háromszor literally stacks "daily" with "three times", the clearest way to state a dose.
